key_insight: Distributionally Robust Schrödinger Bridge learns one stochastic controller that remains effective when the initial distribution shifts, by optimizing worst-case transport performance over an uncertainty set around the nominal start distribution.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for robust generative modeling and control in safety-critical systems where input uncertainty or domain shift can break standard Schrödinger bridge performance.
method: Formulates DRSB as a worst-case control-energy plus terminal KL objective over perturbed initial distributions.
Derives an exact variational form and links the fixed-terminal-cost subproblem to stochastic optimal control and distributionally robust optimization.
Uses an alternating algorithm to update the adversarial initial distribution, estimate terminal log-density ratios, and train the controller, with Wasserstein and Sinkhorn gradient approximations.
evidence_signal: Experiments on 2D transport and image-to-image translation show improved robustness to input perturbations versus standard SB, and Sinkhorn DRSB achieved lower mean sliced Wasserstein distance than fixed noise augmentation on Gaussian mixture transport at two unseen noise levels.
watch_item: The robustness gains come with a tradeoff in nominal performance, and adversarial updates depend on approximating gradients via stochastic control conditions, which may increase implementation complexity.
